reactions.name: Formation of glycolaldehyde
reactions.conditions: Aqueous mineral-catalyzed conditions, potentially involving olivine or alkaline calcium-bearing minerals
reactions.prebiotic_plausibility: Supported by experimental mineral-mediated chemistry, although the reaction is not necessarily selective.

reactions.name: Imine formation
reactions.prebiotic_plausibility: Plausible reversible condensation. The imine need not accumulate or be isolated.

reactions.name: Serine aminonitrile formation
reactions.conditions: Aqueous cyanide chemistry under suitable pH conditions
reactions.prebiotic_plausibility: Experimentally supported. Formation of serine aminonitrile from glycolaldehyde-derived intermediates has been demonstrated.

reactions.name: Nitrile hydration
reactions.conditions: Aqueous hydrolysis, potentially assisted by heating or acidic or alkaline conditions
reactions.prebiotic_plausibility: Chemically established transformation; efficiency under specific prebiotic environments depends on conditions.

reactions.name: Serine formation
reactions.conditions: Warm aqueous conditions with sufficient acid/base catalysis or prolonged hydrolysis
reactions.prebiotic_plausibility: Established hydrolysis chemistry, but the complete sequence has not been demonstrated as a single selective prebiotic process.

pathway_name: Prebiotic Strecker synthesis of serine from formaldehyde
overall_reaction_note: The net equation eliminates ammonia consumed and regenerated in the individual steps.

stereochemistry.explanation: The pathway does not specify an enantioselective mechanism. Formation of the aminonitrile creates a stereocenter and can produce both D- and L-serine.

scientific_limitations: The network combines chemically plausible and experimentally supported transformations, rather than representing a fully validated end-to-end prebiotic experiment.
Formaldehyde condensation generates competing products, and glycolaldehyde can undergo decomposition.
Strecker aminonitrile formation is sensitive to pH and competing reactions.
Nitrile and amide hydrolysis require suitable environmental conditions and may produce side products.
No mechanism for preferential production of L-serine is included.

references.relevance: Experimental formation of serine aminonitrile from a glycolaldehyde-derived intermediate.

references.relevance: Mineral-mediated production of glycolaldehyde from formaldehyde.
